title: RAW UNREVIEWED: an output-shape-indexed recipe compilation separates pictured prototype, material and manufactured part
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A concrete complete medieval recipe distinguishes its morel title, a pear-shaped output, raisin-and-almond material, and a whole almond inserted as a stem. Hypothesize a compilation whose headings or drawings index manufactured shapes rather than literal ingredients. A whole reading must preserve those three roles simultaneously: changing the pictorial prototype must not silently change the material genealogy. No Voynich plant, word or language is assigned.

design.mechanism: The compiler indexes a practical recipe by the object imitated or the final form to be made. The body specifies different actual materials and assigns some of those materials to depicted structural parts. A reader copying such a work could preserve a plant-like design and its shape names even though the instructions are not a botanical description. This is a hypothesis about content organization, not a claim that Voynich depicts confectionery.

actual_source.complete_entry_read: Previously project-exposed source; complete institutional TEI entry read again for this proposal. No new target content accessed.
actual_source.finite_content: Select raisins; pound them; pound peeled almonds with them; add sugar and ginger; form the mixture in the hand like a pear; insert whole almonds below as stems; serve. The morel title, pear analogy and stem analogy do not introduce morels, pears or botanical stems as required ingredients.

prior_positive_evidence: experiments/yolo/gdt341_ordered_recipe_event_graph/SOURCE_AUDIT.md documents this complete recipe family in b4.86, gr1.148 and w1.89; spelling, closure and annotation differ but the shaping and inserted-part sequence recur.

research_registry/proposals/laufenberg_f85r2_20260926/source_supply_20260929/FU_HISTORICAL_REDACTIONS.md independently separates simulated dish names from actual ingredients and distinguishes the two almond roles.
experiments/yolo/gdt791_thirty_page_visual_owner_spine/REPORT.md supplies already inventoried label-versus-prose regimes but no actual Voynich output-shape interpretation.
design.contrast: SHAPE_INDEXED_ARTIFACT: title/picture names a prototype, ingredients constitute another material, final part insertion is literal; BOTANICAL_INPUT: title/picture names the material consumed by the operations; ALL_NAMES_INGREDIENTS: every mentioned object name contributes material. Distinguish these models over the whole record, not a chosen phrase.
design.prediction: The shape-indexed account predicts that both pounded and whole occurrences of one actual material retain material identity but occupy different output roles; the final structural insertion consumes the whole material, not a part harvested from the pictorial prototype. A prototype substitution changes the output-shape and part-placement obligations while retaining ingredient ancestry unless text explicitly changes it. A real material substitution propagates into both affected material roles but does not by itself rename the prototype. These two interventions have different complete written consequences.
design.falsifier: Reject a specified whole reading that uses one occurrence as an ingredient and another as a mere shape analogy without an overt, globally fixed construction distinguishing them; or that needs the pictured prototype as an input although the full recipe constructs it from other named materials. Do not infer physical absence from an unmentioned item. No ingredient, operation or comparator may be supplied by the image alone.
design.smallest_next_step: Author one complete source-bound semantic rendering of b4.86 with MATERIAL, PROTOTYPE and CONSTRUCTED_PART roles, retaining both almond occurrences and all comparison phrases. Compare the complete botanical-input and shape-indexed accounts against the same literal source, then state the exact constructor and incidence consequences a whole Voynich reading would have to express. Only after root selects a separately profiled complete target account should any target be considered. This is a finite content hypothesis, not a graph-retrieval rerun or a new corpus project.
design.predecessors: GDT341 ordered-graph calibration and GDT1159 unknown lexical-graph recovery remain failed; no weight, representation or source panel is repaired. IDEA615 concerns substitutions between source redactions; this asks about role separation inside a single complete source. IDEA711 distinguishes pigment material from surface state and IDEA593 metal identity from misleading appearance; this proposal includes an explicitly constructed multi-part imitation indexed by another object name, with the same ingredient in processed and whole roles. No source image or imitation-Voynich parallel is asserted.
design.limits: The owned example is a recipe, not an illustrated herbal; extending its indexing practice to Voynich is entirely unassessed. Source law is available but target construction binding is not claimed. Current illustrations cannot be relabelled as manufactured objects merely because botanical identification is uncertain. Existing arbitrary historical whole-word glosses are not inherited. Before any word assignment retrieve exact-form frequency, dispersion, grammar and counterexamples; all raw unknowns remain. No f84/f84r, f116v or reserves; no significance or translated name.
